name: Cinematic whoosh-hit: layer sub-whoosh, whoosh and three hit layers, edit the whoosh quieter than the hit and tighten the flam, resample at milestones, dark dual reverbs, upward/parallel compression, clipping, sub removed from the whoosh only, multiband then true-peak limiting
goal: Build a punchy cinematic whoosh-into-hit impact by layering (a reversed sub-kick tail plus a resonant whoosh leading into three short metallic/wooden hits), then editing so the whoosh is quieter than the hit and the hit transients are only slightly flammed, and finishing with a resample-by-milestone processing chain. Delta vs our riser/whoosh variants: the whoosh-to-hit contrast rules (quieter whoosh, no sub in the whoosh) and the clip/limit finishing chain for impacts.

source.title: Sound Design Tutorial: Cinematic Whoosh hit

prerequisites: DAW with audio editing, resampling/bounce and return tracks
Source layers: a synth or recorded sub kick, noise/foley whooshes, 2-3 short impact hits (own recordings or synthesized)
Tape saturation, two reverbs, EQ, multiband/upward compressor, clipper, multiband limiter, true-peak limiter (any brands)

inputs.name: layers
inputs.description: Sub layer, 1-2 whoosh layers, 2-3 hit layers

constraints: Original synthesis/processing recipe; not affiliated with any vendor named in the source. Recreate in browser/Web Audio (Polyrhythm Studio) or any DAW/synth with comparable modules; no presets, banks, impulse responses or samples copied.
The whoosh must be quieter than the hit transient so the hit feels loud by contrast.
Remove sub (below ~60 Hz) from the whoosh so the low end arrives with the hit.
Pitch moves are fixed transpositions of hit layers (lowered pitch), not wobble.
Keep a copy at each resample milestone so you can always go back.
Drums early (Matt's taste): if the track has drums, the kick/drum loop enters by about count 8 (roughly 10-12 s), with only the pad before that.

steps.action: Layer: a sub layer made from the reversed tail of a sub kick, a resonant whoosh layer (e.g. noise or foley swept past a resonant body), and three short hit layers lightly pitched down, each with a small whoosh into a clean transient and a tail.
steps.expect: Five layers that read as whoosh -> hit

steps.action: Resample the sum at the first milestone and keep the original; work on a duplicate.
Edit without plugins: chop the whoosh and lower its level below the hit; trim the hit layers so the transients flam only slightly (a small flam lengthens the body, too much sounds messy).
Resample again, add gentle tape saturation to glue the layers.
Send to two dark reverbs on returns: a room with about 2.75 s decay and a low filter, and a plate with about 3.6 s decay low-passed around 1.4 kHz; sum dry and reverbs into one bus.
steps.expect: Deep, low tail with two characters

steps.action: On the bus: tame the high-end noise in the tail after the transient (adaptive denoise or a dynamic high-shelf cut that acts after the hit), then two upward/downward multiband compressors in series at low mix, then aggressive parallel compression at 50% wet.
steps.expect: Denser, more energetic body without hissy tail

steps.action: Clip the peak hard (about 6 dB of clipping) to square off and prolong the transient, then limit lightly. Resample (milestone 3).

Final pass: re-edit any unwanted whoosh section with fades; high-pass only the whoosh portion at about 60 Hz; a few EQ notches/boosts by ear; light clipping (~1.5 dB); a multiband limiter (lowest band ~0-100 Hz) with some transient emphasis; then a true-peak limiter as a safety net.
steps.tool: EQ + clipper + multiband limiter + true-peak limiter
steps.expect: Punchy, heavy impact that cuts through without digital clipping

verification: Whoosh peak level is clearly below the hit transient level.
No energy below ~60 Hz before the hit; the sub arrives with the hit.
Hit transient shows at most a slight flam.
Final file has no true-peak overs.
